clue.text: Swarm member's place, source of trouble

parts.note: a locus is a place or position

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Asks where a member of a swarm belongs, and blames it for causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts are insects notorious for travelling in vast destructive swarms, so one is a swarm member.

clue.text: Describing Wolves: policy to protect leading position

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a party line is a policy
being up means being ahead, as in a team up by two goals

explanation.surface: Sounds like a report on Wolverhampton Wanderers football club guarding its top spot in the league.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of an English football club, but here it simply means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine is the adjective for wolves, from Latin lupus.

clue.text: Travesty of race had to be sorted out

indicators.note: sorting out means rearranging into a different order

explanation.surface: A shambolic race whose result needed sorting out.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence, a mockery of the real thing, which is a travesty.

clue.text: Swindle seen in tennis camp

indicators.note: something seen inside the next words is sitting among their letters

explanation.surface: A fraud uncovered at a tennis training camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people, a swindle.

clue.text: Change of direction about British Airways headgear

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to turn is to change direction

explanation.surface: A British Airways flight doing a sudden change of course.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a wound cloth head covering, one kind of headgear.

clue.text: In progress subject to control of Washington? Initially yes

parts.note: under as in under someone's authority
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is going ahead under Washington's direction, with a tentative yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something underway has started and is proceeding, which is being in progress.

clue.text: Stark about learner's harsh sound?

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: stark and bare both mean plain and unadorned
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner musician making a bleak, grating noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a loud, harsh noise, like a trumpet or car horn.

clue.text: In the end seen before time? Not quite

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one kept

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they arrived ahead of schedule, and is told not really.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost, falling just short, which is not quite.

clue.text: Notice plea excludes European Queen, for example

indicators.note: excluding something means leaving it out, so one letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
the queen is one of the court cards in a pack

explanation.surface: A legal plea that leaves out a European queen, a hint of royal politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' marks Queen as an instance of something; here a playing card, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A placard is a sign or poster displayed publicly, a notice.

clue.text: Date with donor arranged? Use this perhaps

definitions.note: a pointer to the answer rather than a synonym: 'this' is what you might use

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice before a romantic date: freshen up first.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as a dating tip; the answer is the product you would put on before the date.
explanation.definitionFit: Deodorant is applied to mask body odour, the sort of thing one might use before going out on a date.

clue.text: Doctor regularly avoided bar meal, resulting in scene?

indicators.note: avoiding at regular intervals skips every other letter, keeping the rest

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of bar meal

explanation.surface: A doctor skipping pub lunches, which causes some upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene is causing a commotion, the same sense as making a drama out of something.

clue.text: Patriarch's name, old and historic at the start

indicators.note: only the beginning of each of the preceding words is kept

explanation.surface: Reads as a note that a patriarch's name is ancient and historic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a connector but supplies a letter too: the first letters of name, old, and, historic spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah, builder of the ark in Genesis, is one of the biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Brood over old-fashioned measure that's seen at entrance

indicators.note: in a down-or-across clue, over means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an ell is an obsolete unit of cloth length

explanation.surface: Someone brooding over an outdated unit of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brood' looks like a verb meaning to sulk; it is only letters to be reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorbell is fixed by a front door, so it is a thing that is seen at the entrance of a house.

clue.text: One moving fast in spring term, always last to leave

indicators.note: in each case the final letter departs, so every word is cut short at its end

explanation.surface: A fast runner during the spring school term, never the last to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' tells you the deletion applies to both words, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a runner who races short distances at top speed.

clue.text: Goes ape in broadcast revealing covert activity

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper on air and lets slip a secret operation.
explanation.walkthrough: To go ape is slang for to become wildly angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Espionage is spying, the secret gathering of information, a covert activity.

clue.text: English arriving with four missing jewellery

definitions.note: a mass noun for a single item

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something missing has been taken out, so those letters disappear

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An English person turns up with four pieces of jewellery gone.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is an ornament worn on the earlobe, a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Stress bill just a small amount of money

parts.note: AC is short for account, which a bill is

parts.words: just a small amount of money
parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: Worrying that a bill comes to only a trifling sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' looks like worry in the surface; it is emphasis on a syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the emphasis placed on a syllable or note, which is stress.

clue.text: Take legal action about shoddy stuff in work of art

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to sue is to take someone to court

explanation.surface: Taking someone to court over rubbish passed off as art.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a piece of art.

clue.text: Merrymaking in car, out of order, values half-lost

indicators.note: something out of order is jumbled up, so those letters get rearranged
losing half of a word means dropping half its letters

explanation.surface: Revelry in a broken-down car, with values partly forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a public festival of celebration and revelry, which is merrymaking.

clue.text: Good to participate in means to control period in power

indicators.note: to participate in something is to be inside it, so one letter enters the other word

parts.note: a rein is the strap used to control a horse
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Praising a good way to keep control by joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is the time during which a monarch rules, a period holding power.

clue.text: Good sense to retain Republican's legal document

indicators.note: retaining means holding something inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: wit can mean sound judgement, as in having the wit to do something

explanation.surface: Praises good sense in keeping a Republican's legal papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Republican stands for 'is', linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order issued by a court, a kind of legal document.

clue.text: Perks up initially? Doubly right, there's sign of contentment

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Someone cheering up and twice proved correct, looking pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: The sign of contentment is the sound a happy cat makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A purr is the low vibrating sound a cat makes when it is content.

clue.text: Ruling possessed by medic, thoughtful

indicators.note: something possessed by the following words is held within them, sitting inside their letters

explanation.surface: A doctor carefully issuing a judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or order, a ruling issued by authority.

clue.text: To edges of Ullswater first — this person?

definitions.text: To edges of Ullswater first — this person?

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of Ullswater
1st, with the digit 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Who would head for the shores of Ullswater before anywhere else?
explanation.walkthrough: Ullswater is a lake in England's Lake District, a sightseeing area; the whole clue describes a holidaymaker heading there.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor making for a famous lake first is a sightseer, someone on holiday.

clue.text: Length of time in post — years in a decade, you're talking!

indicators.note: talking means the word is spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: said quickly, you're sounds like the syllable at the word's end

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming that a decade of service in a job is a long stint.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the period for which an office or job is held.

clue.text: Gear up for work in City

indicators.note: letters set to work are put through their paces and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Kitting oneself out for a job in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like the London financial district; it is just any city, here the Czech capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic.
